issues.description: The external seq_tracked_subrange and seq_tracked_map_values helpers return tracked sequences from ordinary ghost sequence inputs without consuming or borrowing the corresponding tracked resources, allowing the same resource model to produce duplicate ownership.
issues.rationale: In proof functions, the unmarked s: Seq<T> input is a ghost value, while the result is explicitly tracked. For a nonempty ghost sequence s representing linear permissions, two calls to seq_tracked_subrange(s, 0, s.len()) both return tracked sequences equal to s, without either call taking a tracked input. seq_tracked_map_values admits the same conversion with an identity mapping. These are external_body promises, so their implementations do not discharge the resource transfer. Segment::split uses the subrange helper for frame-permission owners. The direct child repair removes both ghost-to-tracked axioms and replaces them with seq_tracked_split_at(tracked s: &mut Seq<T>, n), implemented by tracked_pop/tracked_push, transferring each element out of the input sequence. Treat the two axiom signatures as one ghost-to-tracked ownership fabrication root. This is a pre-repair snapshot within the PR, not a claim that this particular intermediate commit first introduced the helpers.
issues.verification: source-only; historical Verus not executed. Read complete helper signatures/bodies, the Segment::split consumer, and direct child repair. The resource-duplication counterexample follows from ghost inputs and tracked outputs; no runtime corruption or historical verifier execution is claimed. Official PR419 commits retrieved in three pages (100+100+51); problem and repair are consecutive and Git parent equality checked.
